root_cause: The dialog opens but focus does not move to the autofocus input because the native <dialog> element does not receive focus when shown via showModal() in this environment, causing focus to remain on the triggering button and then be lost to the body.
repair_strategy: After showing the dialog, explicitly focus the element with the autofocus attribute inside the dialog, falling back to the dialog itself.
expected_accessibility_effect: Focus will move into the dialog and land on the autofocus search field, allowing keyboard users to interact with filters without a pointer.
functional_risks: Potential focus stealing if the dialog already had focus managed elsewhere, but focusing the autofocus element is harmless and aligns with native behavior.
Risk of focusing a non-visible element if the autofocus attribute is misused, though this is unlikely given the DOM structure.
verification_requirements: After opening the drawer via keyboard, focus is on #filters-search.
Pressing Space on #in-stock checkbox toggles its state.
Pressing Tab twice and Enter on #apply updates the applied output to 'in'.
Escape closes drawer and returns focus to #filters-open.
